messages:
alex_r: Heads up — ran the cross-model RoPE safety bench for linear / NTK / YARN across Llama-33B, Mistral-7B, Mixtral-8x22, and Qwen-7B. Saw a surprising perplexity bump on Mixtral-8x22 at 32k context with NTK scaling. Sharing quick numbers and traces.

jamie: ugh, is that the same kernel routing we used for the earlier sweep?

alex_r: Yep same routing policy: prefer fused-attn kernel A -> fallback to KV-sharded kernel B for >16k. Brought the same quantization profile. Results (avg ppl over devset):
```
Model           linear    NTK     YARN
Llama-33B       9.8       9.7     9.9
Mistral-7B      10.5      10.6    10.4
Mixtral-8x22    11.2      13.9    11.5   <-- spike for NTK @ 32k
Qwen-7B         10.1      10.0    10.2
```

alex_r: CPU/GPU perf counters show an increase in memcopy/PCI stalls when Mixtral NTK hits ~24k tokens and again at ~30k. KV cache growth looks fine size-wise but get more small, fragmented CUDA memcpy ops.

perf-bot: profile-summary: mixtral_ntk_32k: native_kernel_time=62ms, memcpy_total=18ms, memcpy_ops=342, kernel_switches=7

sasha: that memcpy_ops number is suspiciously high. Could be our KV layout for Mixtral (head_kv dim mismatch) causing many tiny copies. Did you use packed KV layout or per-shard?

alex_r: packed per-device — same codepath used for other models, but Mixtral's head/kvdim is 128 vs others 64, and heads=32 vs 16. Maybe our batch heuristic for chunky batching creates many tiny KV writes because we switch to stale KV flush earlier.

jamie: also check the RoPE exponent scaling we apply. For NTK we scale down position multipliers differently; if kernel B assumes different pre-scaling, we might be re-transforming KV between kernels which triggers copies.

alex_r: good call. I dumped kernel selection trace:
```
[0..16k] -> kernelA_fused
[16k..24k] -> kernelB_kv_shard (repack)
[24k..32k] -> kernelB_kv_shard (repack)
```
Each transition calls repack_kv_for_kernel which does an allocate + cudaMemcpy per-device. That explains the memcpy ops.

talia_m: Could we avoid repack by introducing a compatible alias layout for Mixtral (increase head_kv stride)? Maybe a small shim in kernelB to accept both layouts with a bool flag.

sasha: shim might be fastest short-term. Longer term: improve batching heuristic to avoid triggering kernel boundary mid-request. If a request is long (e.g., >20k) force a single kernel path by selecting kernelB from the start. That reduces repack count to 0 but might change latency profile for <16k.

jamie: we should also sanity-check quality regression — is the ppl spike purely perf artifact or does repack/rounding change values? Could memcpy ordering / alignment affect fp16 quantization noise?

alex_r: I compared logits before/after repack for a few examples: differences are tiny (L2 norm ~ 1e-4) — seems numeric noise only. Perplexity bump persists on full devset, so it's likely due to edge-case in RoPE NTK implementation interacting with Mixtral's attention head geometry.

sasha: remind me — Mixtral uses per-head RoPE scale factor variant right? That interacts with NTK since we apply exponent per-dim. Maybe our per-head scaling table is being indexed with head count assumption from linear variant, causing an off-by-stride for NTK path.

alex_r: I reviewed the code: rotate_mult table computed with heads from model.cfg, but kernelB's vectorized load assumes contiguous heads with stride equal to kv_dim/8. For Mixtral that assumption is broken when kv_dim not divisible by 8 on some sharding configs. So read misaligned memory -> small corruption -> higher ppl.

talia_m: OK that explains quality regression. Fix path: 1) Make kernelB loads robust to arbitrary head_kv dim (minor perf hit) 2) Add batching heuristic to prefer single kernel for long requests 3) Add a repack-free alias path for Mixtral to keep perf.

jamie: prioritized tasks? I'd do (1) asap since correctness > perf. Then a short experiment for (2) to measure latency/cost tradeoffs. (3) can be an optimization later.

alex_r: agreed. I'll open a PR for kernelB robustness and a follow-up perf PR for batching heuristic. I'll attach a micro-benchmark and the perf-bot profiles.

perf-bot: created perf-issue #4287 for mixtral_ntk_32k with attached traces.

sasha: one more note — when you tune batching heuristic, please test with our continuous-batching mode and with burst-mode enabled; the interaction with prefix caching changes the memcopy pattern.

alex_r: will do. ETA: kernel fix PR today, batching experiment tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:

jamie: thanks — keep us posted.
